Apple recalls Beats Pill speakers over overheating batteries

Published 2026-10-07 15:10 UTC

Apple is recalling roughly 200,000 Beats Pill portable speakers sold since June because the lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging, according to a notice from the US Consumer Product Safety Commission. Apple says it has received 31 reports of speakers getting hot, including four that caused minor burns.

Owners should stop using the speaker and request a free replacement or a full refund through the Beats support site. The recall covers speakers in black, champagne and red with serial numbers starting with the letters BP.

This is the second Beats recall in two years. Apple bought Beats in 2014 and still sells the brand's headphones and speakers alongside AirPods. The company said the problem was traced to a faulty charging circuit from a single supplier and has been fixed in new units.

The recall covers speakers sold in the United States, Canada and Europe between March and August of this year. Apple said it has received 87 reports of batteries overheating, including six reports of minor burns and two reports of damage to furniture. No serious injuries have been reported.

Owners can check whether their speaker is affected by entering its serial number on Apple's support site. The affected units have serial numbers within a specific range printed on the bottom of the speaker near the charging port. Apple asks customers to stop using and charging affected speakers immediately.

Customers will receive a full refund or a replacement speaker from a newer production batch, along with a prepaid shipping box to return the recalled unit. Apple stores and authorized retailers will also accept returns. The company said it identified a manufacturing defect in a battery component supplied by one vendor and has changed suppliers.

Consumer safety regulators said lithium-ion battery recalls have become more common as portable electronics multiply. They advise people not to leave charging devices unattended on beds or sofas, where heat cannot escape, and to dispose of damaged batteries at proper recycling points rather than in household trash.
